author: WP07
summary: Follows a draw from public vertex values through declarations, buffers and bindings (semantic composition, minimum-offset fold, validation order) and explains what capability answers, interface defaults and the unsupported-3D policy do and do not guarantee. Partly stale at TARGET: 19 capability members (not 13), null bindings refused, repeated semantics remapped rather than dropped, InvalidOperationException for a missing effect, renderer-dependent range validation, a non-zero element hash and more stream sizes. Tutorial 101 already carried the capability table, polarity and policy; the vertex contract, interface-default shapes and portable-claim checklist were missing and form two new deep dives.

concepts.text: The shared renderer interface mixes useful defaults, explicit refusals, silent no-ops and an effect-discarding draw fallback, so a draw must be followed from public vertex values through declarations and bindings to what a capability answer does and does not guarantee.

concepts.section: Public vertex objects are not upload layouts
concepts.text: CNA's public vertex types and Color are polymorphic (IVertexType with a virtual destructor, IPackedVector), so a vertex object carries a virtual-table pointer and its C++ layout is not the GPU stream layout.

concepts.section: Public vertex objects are not upload layouts
concepts.text: The plain stream structs in BuiltInVertexStreams.hpp have asserted sizes 16, 20, 24, 32, 48, 52, 60, 68, 76 and 80 bytes (the chapter lists seven sizes), and each built-in declaration takes its stride from sizeof and offsets from offsetof.
concepts.note: Corrected: 60, 76 and 80-byte streams exist at TARGET.

concepts.section: Public vertex objects are not upload layouts
concepts.text: Typed VertexBuffer::SetData for the seven built-in types and DrawUserPrimitives pack public values into the stream form through one Pack() per type.

concepts.section: Public vertex objects are not upload layouts
concepts.text: The template SetData<TVertex> copies bytes verbatim and static_asserts a trivially copyable type, so a custom vertex struct deriving from IVertexType is rejected; write a plain struct plus an explicit VertexDeclaration.

concepts.section: Public vertex objects are not upload layouts
concepts.text: SetDataRaw reads exactly count x stride caller bytes; the stride must equal the declaration's and the source extent is the caller's promise — passing polymorphic objects through void* does not produce the XNA stride.
A VertexDeclaration's layout is immutable after construction; each element stores offset, format, usage and usage index, and the stride is explicit or the largest offset plus format size.
The element-list constructors throw ArgumentNullException for an empty list; a non-positive explicit stride throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException.

Construction also requires a stride that is a multiple of four, element usages in range, elements inside the stride at four-byte-aligned offsets, no repeated (usage, usage index) pair and no byte overlap.
The CNAEXT default constructor creates an empty zero-stride declaration for the legacy VertexBuffer(device, count) path, exempt from validation, whose renderer uses its own upload stride.

ValidateForProfile runs at VertexBuffer creation and for user-array draws: stride at most 255 bytes, at most 16 elements, usage index 0-15, Reach formats Single..NormalizedShort4 and HiDef adding HalfVector2/HalfVector4.

The declaration reaches every renderer through the pure-virtual IVertexBufferRenderer::SetVertexDeclaration; the older description that CNA selects layouts from stride alone is obsolete, though renderers still optimise known built-in layouts.

Faithful paths bind declared elements: Vulkan refuses a declaration missing a stock program input before queueing, Software reads by semantic with a stride fallback only for undeclared buffers, GL renderers bind custom programs by element index.

target.evidence: draw-call internals (RequireFaithfulDeclarationEXT; Software stride list); EasyGLRenderer.cpp

concepts.text: VertexElement is mutable; the chapter says its hash returns zero, but at TARGET GetHashCode() XORs the four 32-bit fields (zero mapped to INT32_MAX) as XNA hashes value types — still weak, so compare full element sequences and stride for cache keys.
concepts.note: Corrected: the hash is not zero at TARGET; the cache-key advice stands.

concepts.text: Copies of a VertexDeclaration share one resource identity, as references to one object do in C#.

concepts.section: Buffers, index widths, and dynamic updates
concepts.text: VertexBuffer stores a declaration, vertex count, usage and renderer resource; copy is deleted and move is noexcept so a native handle is never duplicated.

concepts.section: Buffers, index widths, and dynamic updates
concepts.text: Typed transfer families cover the seven built-in stream shapes; the CNAEXT raw route takes a pointer, element count and stride.

concepts.section: Buffers, index widths, and dynamic updates
concepts.text: IndexBuffer has 16-bit and 32-bit SetData/GetData families plus a byte-exact SetData<T> template; Reach refuses 32-bit index buffers and user indices; both buffer kinds are limited to 67,108,863 bytes.

concepts.section: Buffers, index widths, and dynamic updates
concepts.text: IndexElementSize uses XNA's ordinals but content formats encode width differently (the XNB model reader maps an element byte size of 2 to SixteenBits), so tools must translate the 16/32 meaning, not copy an ordinal.

concepts.section: Buffers, index widths, and dynamic updates
concepts.text: Dynamic buffers add a content-lost surface and SetDataOptions overloads; the typed (data, startIndex, elementCount, options) overloads always write from the buffer's start, but XNA-shaped offsetInBytes overloads write at an offset (the chapter says the destination always begins at zero).
concepts.note: Corrected: offset overloads exist at TARGET.

concepts.section: Buffers, index widths, and dynamic updates
concepts.text: SetDataOptions act as a native update-strategy hint (orphaning for Discard, unsynchronised write for NoOverwrite) on most renderers; a few treat every call like Discard.

concepts.section: Buffers, index widths, and dynamic updates
concepts.text: IsContentLost becomes true only when a renderer reports a real device reset (DIRECTX9/11/12, DIRECT2D, WEBGPU emit the event) and is cleared by SetData; on renderers that cannot lose a device it stays false.

target.evidence: GraphicsDevice.cpp (deviceEventCallback Reset -> NotifyContentLostResourcesEXT); renderer deviceEventCallback_ calls

concepts.note: Refined: the chapter says it remains false in normal operation.

concepts.section: Buffers, index widths, and dynamic updates
concepts.text: A bound buffer cannot be rewritten without Discard/NoOverwrite; CPU shadows and readback are documented with the buffer page.

concepts.section: Bindings carry offset and input rate
concepts.text: VertexBufferBinding combines buffer, VertexOffset and InstanceFrequency; frequency 0 is per-vertex, positive is per-instance; the constructor refuses a null buffer, an offset outside [0, VertexCount) or a negative frequency.

concepts.section: Bindings carry offset and input rate
concepts.text: SetVertexBuffers accepts at most 16 bindings ('Max Vertex Buffers supported is 16.').

concepts.section: Bindings carry offset and input rate
concepts.text: The chapter says SetVertexBuffers permits null buffers as unused slots; at TARGET a null binding throws ArgumentException, following Microsoft XNA rather than FNA, and a failure keeps the prefix processed before it.
concepts.note: Corrected: nulls are refused at TARGET.

concepts.section: Bindings carry offset and input rate
concepts.text: The public 16-binding ceiling is not proof that the selected renderer can consume sixteen active streams.

concepts.section: Bindings carry offset and input rate
concepts.text: The classic shapes need no capability: one per-vertex binding, and one per-vertex plus one per-instance binding.
tokens: one per-vertex stream plus one per-instance stream

concepts.section: Bindings carry offset and input rate
concepts.text: More than one stream of the same rate requires MultiStreamVertexInput; a false answer throws NotSupportedException naming the counts before native submission instead of rendering from stream 0.
tokens: naming the per-vertex and per-instance stream counts

concepts.section: Bindings carry offset and input rate
concepts.text: A stream count above the renderer's GetMaxVertexStreams() (16 by default; Vulkan the device limit) also throws; the list is never silently truncated.

concepts.section: Bindings carry offset and input rate
concepts.text: The chapter says a later fully duplicated stream contributes nothing and a partially repeating one is rejected; at TARGET repeated (usage, index) pairs across streams are moved to the first free index of the same usage (FNA3D driver rule), every stream is kept, and only exhausting all 16 indices throws.
concepts.note: Corrected: remapping, not dropping or rejecting.

concepts.section: Bindings carry offset and input rate
concepts.text: The stream table records each buffer's VertexCount as capacity, not the last SetData length, because XNA lets a game rewrite a prefix of a larger buffer.

concepts.section: Bindings carry offset and input rate
concepts.text: Only streams the stock program actually consumes are range-checked; per-instance and legacy empty-declaration streams always count as consumed.

With several per-vertex bindings CNA folds the smallest VertexOffset once into vertexStart or baseVertex (saturating add) and each stream keeps its non-negative remainder; renderers multiply by each stream's own stride, so strides need not match.
Folding each full offset into one base would apply the minimum several times; dropping remainders would align only the earliest stream.
With one stream the fold is byte-identical to the older single-offset behaviour.

A per-instance stream keeps its whole offset because baseVertex never advances it; the instanced route validates each consumed per-instance stream (1 + lastInstance / frequency records after its offset).
The normalisation lives in the shared layer so every renderer sees the same binding geometry; OrdinaryDrawBindingOffsetTests and OrdinaryDrawMultiStreamTests pin it.

concepts.section: Draw validation has a deliberate order
concepts.text: Every buffer-backed 3D draw first asks the renderer to enforce its 3D policy (Ensure3DSupported), before any argument is examined.

concepts.section: Draw validation has a deliberate order
concepts.text: The chapter says missing effect state is a plain std::runtime_error; at TARGET a missing effect, index buffer or vertex buffer is InvalidOperationException and a disposed bound buffer ObjectDisposedException.

concepts.section: Draw validation has a deliberate order
concepts.text: Range validation precedes capability validation, so an out-of-range request is an argument error before a capability error.

concepts.section: Draw validation has a deliberate order
concepts.text: The chapter says range failures are identical on every renderer; at TARGET the managed range guard applies only where RequiresManagedBufferedDrawRangeValidationEXT() is true — EasyGL, OPENGL4 and SOFTWARE forward ranges to the native API as XNA does — and always on the legacy empty-declaration route.

concepts.section: Draw validation has a deliberate order
concepts.text: Profile checks come early: positive counts, 65,535 primitives per draw on Reach and 1,048,575 on HiDef, and the topology-derived element count.

concepts.section: Draw validation has a deliberate order
concepts.text: User-array draws follow the same stages: validate, require an effect, pack typed values, upload a transient buffer carrying the type's canonical declaration (as FNA's declaration cache does), fill GpuDrawParams, enter the renderer; the VertexPositionColor overload forces vertex colour on.

The chapter's thirteen-entry table is stale: GraphicsCapability has 19 append-only members at TARGET (C ABI values 0-18), adding CompiledEffects (already at alpha.1) and the float/half-float targets, half-float filtering, compute and indirect draw.

Each member asks a CNA contract question (3D pipeline, real depth/stencil attachment, stencil independent of depth, MSAA, wireframe, anisotropy, genuine additive path, MRT, real occlusion query, float targets, half-float filtering, multi-stream, distinct instance records, indirect draws, compiled effects, compute) rather than exposing a native feature bit.
CustomEffects is defined by its header as a non-stock Effect passed to SpriteBatch::Begin(); source execution is a separate detailed-profile feature.
Texture3D promises real volume storage and transfer, never shader sampling (a separate profile feature).

Narrow renderers answer honestly without GPU semantics: SOFTWARE bounded CPU Texture3D storage, GDI a 2D stencil mask without depth, HTML_DOM additive blending depending on browser plus-lighter support.

IGraphicsRenderer::SupportsCapability returns true by default except StencilBuffer (delegated), MultiStreamVertexInput (false), CompiledEffects (opt-in hook) and the float render-target entries (false) — the chapter lists only the first two exceptions.
tokens: returns true for every member except four

concepts.text: Opt-out spares mature renderers boilerplate, but a new or narrow renderer that forgets an override overclaims; DIRECTX9 is the only family with no override at TARGET.
Six members are derived at device level from false-by-default hooks and MRT is ANDed with the profile limit, so the device answer fails closed for them; ask the device, not the renderer interface.
tokens: Ask the device, not the renderer interface

concepts.text: Answers are configuration- and host-sensitive: SDL_GPU occlusion false, compiled effects and SDL_GPU custom effects vary with options/libshaderc, FNA3D compiled yes but custom false, HEADLESS ThreeD true without pixels.
tokens: describes one build on one device

concepts.text: A capability check is necessary but not sufficient for known report/path mismatches (DIRECTX9 custom-effect declaration, Vulkan/SDL_GPU dialect features, missing IndirectDraw name in the engine layer, stale compute comment); pair the query with the operation and an observable oracle.
tokens: necessary but, for these entries, not sufficient

concepts.text: The detailed RendererCapabilityProfile (32 features, four-state answers, 22 limits, per-format masks where a missing known bit means unclassified) separates what the Booleans merge.

The feature-matrix appendix pairs capability answers with operational evidence rather than copying a Boolean as support; at TARGET the site's renderer capability matrix and evidence tables serve that role.
concepts.note: The site's code-derived per-identity matrix supersedes the book's appendix cross-reference.

concepts.section: Unsupported 3D policy is separate from capability
concepts.text: Unsupported3DGraphicsCallBehavior has Throw (default, the renderer's established refusal) and WarnAndStub (log once per method, return a safe no-op or null-object resource where defined).

concepts.section: Unsupported 3D policy is separate from capability
concepts.text: Changing the policy to a different value clears the warn-once history; setting the same value does nothing.

concepts.section: Unsupported 3D policy is separate from capability
concepts.text: The policy does not change capability answers and does not suppress invalid arguments, disposed resources, driver failures or unfinished work on a renderer that claims 3D.

concepts.section: Unsupported 3D policy is separate from capability
concepts.text: There is no environment variable for the policy; applications opt in per device through GraphicsDevice::SetUnsupported3DGraphicsCallBehavior.

concepts.section: Unsupported 3D policy is separate from capability
concepts.text: Only DIRECT2D, HTML_DOM and SVG_DOM override the early Ensure3DSupported hook; other 2D families refuse in capability, factory or draw methods, so an absent override is not evidence of 3D support.

target.evidence: grep Ensure3DSupported in modules/renderers (direct2d, html-dom, svg-dom)

concepts.section: Unsupported 3D policy is separate from capability
concepts.text: Only SDL_RENDERER, CANVAS, FREEDIRECT and DIRECT2D honour WarnAndStub; GDI, HTML_DOM and SVG_DOM always throw.

Effect-discarding fallback: the default DrawPrimitivesEx/DrawIndexedPrimitivesEx drop GpuDrawParams and call the coloured route; at TARGET only SDL_RENDERER, DIRECT2D, CANVAS, HTML_DOM, SVG_DOM, FREEDIRECT and STUB inherit it and their coloured routes refuse or no-op — every 3D family overrides both.

target.evidence: IGraphicsRenderer.hpp (DrawPrimitivesEx default); grep DrawPrimitivesEx in modules/renderers/*

concepts.text: An earlier, larger renderer set contained a family that drew a plausible untextured image through the effect-discarding fallback; the lesson applies to any new renderer.

target.evidence: historical (retired family, name withheld by policy)

concepts.note: Retired family not named per policy.

concepts.text: Hard refusal: the default instanced draw throws std::runtime_error (or warns under WarnAndStub on a 2D renderer) and default back-buffer readback throws.

Silent no-op: about fifty virtual methods have empty bodies (including IEffectRenderer uniform setters), so a public call can update a cache while no native state changes unless the shared setter guards it.

Null factory: CreateOcclusionQuery, CreateTexture3D, CreateTextureCube, CreateRenderTarget2D and CreateEffectRenderer default to null; the wrapper refuses (OcclusionQuery throws NotSupportedException), degrades or exposes an inert object.
The renderer contract header is over four thousand lines (the chapter says over two thousand), and families must be classified by where calls actually end, not by override counts.

'The triangle rendered' is incomplete; a durable claim names the identity and family, declaration, stride, index width and binding rates, capability answers with known mismatches, the applied effect and whether GpuDrawParams was consumed, the native driver/host, and the discriminating oracle.
With those nouns present, a failure can be localised to packing, binding normalisation, capability reporting, effect dispatch or native rendering.
GetGraphicsRendererName() reports the renderer that really started in a multi-renderer build, not the build default.
